title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 71-73): Grothendieck seeks an intrinsic, characteristic-free characterization of the Schwarzian derivative and of the sheaf of projective structures on a curve. This is presumably tied to the Picard-Fuchs and uniformization themes of this folder.

I (previous page). X is a complex analytic curve. E_X (resp. P_X) is the sheaf of local étale maps to A^1 (resp. P^1). One looks for G: E_X x E_X -> ω^{⊗2} satisfying:
(a) G is a (nonlinear) differential operator, rational in the jets of f and g.
(b) G is a cocycle: G(f,g) + G(g,h) = G(f,h).
(c) G is invariant under the affine maps and under g -> 1/g on the second argument, i.e. under PGL_2(C).
(d) A rigidity condition: if G(f,g) = 0 and f, g agree to order 2 at a point, then f = g on a connected U.
On a fixed X, G is unique up to a unit φ ∈ Γ(X, O*). If X is allowed to vary along étale morphisms (II), G is unique up to a constant c ∈ C*.

This page, top bracket. Functoriality for étale maps forces the rational function R to have constant coefficients, independent of X. Moreover its denominator is a monomial F_1^p G_1^q, so G = P(f,...,g,...)/(f'^p g'^q).
A solution is C(f,g) = ([-2 g'''/g' + 3(g''/g')^2] - [same for f]) dt^2, which equals 2(S(f) - S(g)) dt^2, where S is the classical Schwarzian.
There is a canonical torsor T_X under ω^{⊗2}, functorial for étale maps, with a map c^X: P_X -> T_X satisfying C(f,g) = c^X(g) - c^X(f). The map c^X factors through H\P_X, with H = PGL_2(C), and the induced map H\P_X -> T_X is an isomorphism. In modern terms, T_X is the torsor of projective connections (projective structures), and c^X sends a local coordinate to its projective structure.

III (arithmetic version). X/S is a smooth relative curve over an arbitrary scheme S. One asks for C: E_X x E_X -> ω^2_{X/S}, compatible with base change S' -> S and with étale X' -> X over S, satisfying the analogues of (a)-(d).
Ordinary derivatives are replaced by divided-power (Hasse-Schmidt) derivatives D_t^{(i)}. Varying X forces the coefficients to lie in Z, or in Γ(S, O_S) over a fixed base. A solution exists and is unique up to ε ∈ Z* = {±1}.
The classical C vanishes identically in characteristics 2 and 3, so one must take C_0 = C/12:
C_0(f,g) = [(-D^{(3)}g/D^{(1)}g + (D^{(2)}g/D^{(1)}g)^2) - (same for f)] dt^2.
Check: D^{(2)} = d^2/2 and D^{(3)} = d^3/6. Hence -D3/D1 + (D2/D1)^2 = (1/12)(-2 f'''/f' + 3(f''/f')^2) = -S(f)/6. So C_0 = (S(f) - S(g))/6 with integral coefficients; S/6 is the integral normalization of the Schwarzian.
To fix the sign, Grothendieck evaluates C_0(t,t^2) and C_0(t,t^3). He notes that t^2 is never étale in characteristic 2, so denominators are harmless. He also notes that sign-fixing is pointless in characteristic 2, where ±1 coincide.

Rem 1. If one replaces ω^{⊗2} by an arbitrary coherent target F, every such C factors uniquely as u∘C with u: ω^{⊗2} -> F. So ω^{⊗2} is the universal target.
The next page adds two points. First, the torsor T^{φG} is the push-out of T^G along multiplication by φ, so T^{C} is 12 times T^{C_0}. Second, the char-p characterization is posed only as a question: uniqueness up to F_p^*, or up to Γ(S, O_S^*) over a non-reduced base.
errors: The computation C_0(t,t^2) should give D^{(1)}t^2 = 2t, D^{(2)}t^2 = 1, D^{(3)} = 0, hence C_0(t,t^2) = (1/(2t))^2 dt^2 = 1/(4t^2) dt^2. The value '1/(2t) dt^2' in the transcription is either a misreading or a slip in the manuscript; the struck-out fragment may be the correct value.

C_0(t,t^3) = (-1/(3t^2) + 1/t^2) dt^2 = (2/3)(1/t^2) dt^2 is correct. Note that 2/3 ≡ 0 mod 2, so in characteristic 2 this test value vanishes. This is consistent with his remark that the sign test is useless there.

Gap: the claims that the coefficients must be constants in C (resp. in Z), that the denominator is a monomial in f' and g', and the existence/uniqueness up to ±1 over Spec Z are asserted, not proved. In particular, the role of condition (d) in characteristic p (where many functions have vanishing derivatives) is not addressed; he raises this on the next page.
Normalization: C = 2(S(f) - S(g)) in the classical convention S = f'''/f' - (3/2)(f''/f')^2. The sign convention is opposite to the usual cocycle S(g∘f^{-1}) convention, but this is harmless.

ideas.what: Characterization of the Schwarzian as the unique (up to constant) Möbius-invariant differential-operator cocycle E_X x E_X -> ω^{⊗2} satisfying a rigidity condition, functorial in étale maps
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative as the PGL_2-invariant 1-cocycle on (local) diffeomorphisms with values in quadratic differentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Cayley); cocycle and uniqueness viewpoint via Gelfand-Fuchs and Bott-Thurston; uniqueness statements e.g. Ovsienko-Tabachnikov

ideas.what: Canonical ω^{⊗2}-torsor T_X with PGL_2\P_X ≅ T_X (the sheaf of projective structures as a torsor under quadratic differentials)
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of projective connections / projective structures (sl_2-opers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1960s), Hubbard; Deligne (1970, Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers); Beilinson-Drinfeld (opers)

ideas.what: Arithmetic Schwarzian over Z using Hasse-Schmidt derivatives, -D^{(3)}f/D^{(1)}f + (D^{(2)}f/D^{(1)}f)^2 = -S(f)/6, with existence and uniqueness up to sign for all smooth curves over all bases
ideas.modern_name: Integral/characteristic-free Schwarzian; projective structures in positive and mixed characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara ('Schwarzian equations', 1974) for char-p Schwarzian themes; Mochizuki (indigenous bundles, 1990s); Hoshi (Frobenius-projective structures); Wakabayashi (dormant opers)

ideas.what: Universality of ω^{⊗2} as the target: any such cocycle with values in a coherent F factors uniquely through ω^{⊗2}
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the quadratic differential sheaf for invariant cocycles

ideas.what: Comparison of torsors under rescaling: T^{φG} is the push-out of T^G by φ, so the classical torsor is 12 times the integral one
ideas.modern_name: Change of structure group of torsors under multiplication by a scalar

missed.claim: A characterization theorem over Spec Z: for smooth relative curves X/S, compatibly with base change and étale maps, there is a unique (up to ±1) PGL_2-invariant differential cocycle E_X x E_X -> ω^{⊗2}_{X/S}. It is given by the Hasse-derivative expression -D3/D1 + (D2/D1)^2, i.e. S/6, and the classical normalization must be divided by 12 because it vanishes identically in characteristics 2 and 3.
missed.quote: On trouve encore l'existence d'un tel, et l'unicité à un facteur ε∈Z* près, i.e. ε=±1 : unicité au signe près! Ici, on ne peut prendre l'expression C(f,g) précédente, car elle est identiquement nulle en car. 2 et 3! Il faut prendre 1/12 C(f,g)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and char-p projective structures (Ihara, Mochizuki, Hoshi, Wakabayashi) usually work with p odd or with opers. An explicit uniqueness-up-to-sign characterization of the integral Schwarzian, uniform over all of Spec Z including p = 2, 3, would be a clean foundational statement I do not recall seeing stated this way.

missed.claim: He asks whether the integral Schwarzian is characterized in characteristic p (up to F_p^*, or up to Γ(S, O_S^*) over a non-reduced S) by the conditions a), b), c) plus a modified rigidity condition d'), and does not settle it.
missed.quote: On pourrait se poser la question de caractériser c_0(f,g) par une caractéristique dominée p>0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In characteristic p, condition (d) fails naively because of p-th powers. The right rigidity condition is exactly where Frobenius-projective / dormant structures enter, which is relevant to Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory.

missed.claim: The page links the torsor of projective structures (an ω^{⊗2}-torsor, with a canonical 12-fold relation between the classical and integral normalizations) to the Gauss-Manin/Picard-Fuchs/Cartier-operator context of this folder.
missed.quote: De plus, on trouve un torseur canonique T_X sous ω^{⊗2}_{X/C}, dépendant fonctoriellement de X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early algebraic, characteristic-free treatment of the projective-structure torsor, contemporaneous with Ihara's Schwarzian equations. It is relevant historically to the origins of indigenous bundles and opers in arithmetic.

deep.surprise_reason: The complex-analytic part is classical. The arithmetic version — the Schwarzian over Spec Z via Hasse derivatives, the forced 1/12 normalization because of characteristics 2 and 3, and uniqueness up to sign — is a neat, apparently unpublished observation dating from ~1972. It anticipates later char-p projective-structure work, but it is modest and stated without proof.
transcription_corrections: 'Ici, on montre que la condition a) implique que' — the interlinear insertion replaces the struck 'pour tt X fixé'.
The value of C_0(t,t^2) should mathematically be 1/(4t^2) dt^2; the '1/(2t) dt^2' reading is suspect, either a misreading or Grothendieck's slip.
'c^X se factorise en H\P_X → T_X': H denotes PGL_2(C) acting on P_X (a quotient, written with a left subscript H).
In the denominator of R, the exponents are unknown powers p, q: F_1^p G_1^q, consistent with the previous page.
'X lisse (variété lisse de dimension relative 1)' — 'dimension relative' rather than 'dimension'; 'courbe lisse sur S'.
